issues.legal_issue: No further appeal is available from a State Commission order made in an appeal concerning penal enforcement, except through the appellate route expressly provided by law.
material_facts: The State Commission set aside the District Forum’s conviction and sentence in proceedings for non-compliance with a consumer forum order.
The National Commission dismissed the ensuing appeal, holding that no second appeal was provided against the State Commission’s order.
issues.conclusion: The National Commission correctly held that it had no jurisdiction to entertain a second appeal from the State Commission’s order under the statutory appeal scheme.
issues.legal_principle: Section 27A(1) of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 specifies the appeal route for orders under Section 27, including an appeal from the State Commission to the National Commission. Section 27A(2) excludes other appeals from orders of the District Forum, State Commission, or National Commission. The Court also held that Section 21 did not provide a basis to entertain the second appeal. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.consumer_penal_enforcement_appeal: The proceeding concerns an appeal about penal enforcement of a consumer forum order.
predicates.state_commission_decided_the_first_appea: The State Commission decided the first appeal in that proceeding.

issues.definition: When a State Commission decides the first appeal in a consumer penal-enforcement proceeding, no second appeal lies from its order.

issues.legal_issue: A consumer forum imposing a penalty for disobedience must afford the accused an opportunity to be heard and follow the applicable summary-trial procedure.
material_facts: The District Forum convicted and sentenced the officers for non-compliance with its order.
The State Commission found that the District Forum had not followed the summary-trial procedure and had not afforded the officers an opportunity to be heard.
issues.conclusion: Penal action for non-compliance had to be taken only after following the applicable summary-trial procedure and affording the respondents an opportunity to be heard.
issues.legal_principle: Section 27(3) of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 requires the prescribed procedure for penal proceedings. The Court directed the District Forum to follow Section 262 read with Chapter XX and Section 251 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.consumer_penal_proceeding: A consumer forum is conducting a proceeding to impose a penalty for disobedience of its order.
predicates.accused_not_given_opportunity_to_be_hear: The persons facing penal action were not afforded an opportunity to be heard.

issues.definition: If a consumer forum conducts a penal proceeding without giving the accused an opportunity to be heard, the penal action must be conducted using the applicable summary-trial procedure.

issues.legal_issue: A consumer forum’s order setting aside a procedurally defective penal order should be accompanied by a remand for lawful further proceedings where failure to remand would defeat enforcement of a final consumer order.
material_facts: The original order in favour of the consumer had attained finality and remained uncomplied with.
The State Commission set aside the District Forum’s penal order because the required procedure had not been followed, but did not remand the matter.
The consumer had been pursuing enforcement for many years, and the Court considered that not remanding the case would cause the right secured by the original order to be lost.
issues.conclusion: The Court modified the State Commission’s order to remand the matter to the District Forum for lawful enforcement and penal proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: The Court exercised its power under Article 142 of the Constitution of India to prevent the consumer’s accrued right from being lost and directed a remand for proceedings in accordance with the Code of Criminal Procedure. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: consumer_order_enforcement_proceeding and underlying_consumer_order_is_final and penal_order_set_aside_for_procedural_defect and no_remand_would_defeat_enforcement

predicates.consumer_order_enforcement_proceeding: The proceeding concerns enforcement of an order made by a consumer forum.
predicates.underlying_consumer_order_is_final: The underlying consumer forum order has attained finality.
predicates.penal_order_set_aside_for_procedural_def: A penal order for disobedience was set aside because required procedure was not followed.
predicates.no_remand_would_defeat_enforcement: Without a remand, the consumer’s ability to obtain the benefit of the final order would be lost.

issues.definition: When a final consumer order remains to be enforced and a penal order is set aside for procedural defects, the matter must be remanded if not doing so would defeat enforcement.

issues.legal_issue: A consumer forum may use civil execution procedures, including the procedure for enforcing an order requiring a person to perform an act, to execute its final orders where those procedures have not been excluded.
material_facts: The District Forum’s final order required the consumer society to provide and register the allotted plot in the consumer’s favour.
The order had not been complied with, and the consumer sought execution.
The Court considered the consumer forum’s order to be in the nature of a decree and found no express or implied exclusion of the relevant civil execution procedure.
issues.conclusion: The consumer could invoke the Code of Civil Procedure, including Order XXI Rule 32, to seek execution of the District Forum’s order.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 13(4), 13(6), and 13(7) of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 support the applicability of the Code of Civil Procedure to proceedings before the District Forum. In the absence of an express or implied exclusion, Order XXI Rule 32 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 may be used to execute a consumer forum order that is in the nature of a decree and requires performance of an act. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.consumer_forum_execution_proceeding: The proceeding is before a consumer forum for execution of its order.
predicates.final_order_requires_performance_of_an_a: The final order requires a person to perform an act for the benefit of the successful consumer.
predicates.civil_execution_procedure_not_excluded: The applicable framework does not expressly or impliedly exclude the relevant civil execution procedure.

issues.definition: A consumer forum may use civil execution procedure to enforce a final order requiring performance of an act when that procedure has not been excluded.
